skeleton: The signature is consistent with an early-fault precursor: the underlying dynamics fit {motif_label}, and {anomaly_count} excursions sit outside the expected envelope. In industrial monitoring this is exactly when scheduling matters — fault probability is rising, time-to-failure is finite, and a planned maintenance window is dramatically cheaper than reactive repair.

A regime change is visible in the sensor stream. For an industrial system this most often signals one of: a maintenance event, a load-profile shift, or component wear crossing a threshold. The next step is the maintenance log — Aurora can confirm the timing of the shift but the operational context decides which of the three causes applies.

The system shows a damped oscillator signature consistent with {motif_label}. For mechanical components this is the resonance fingerprint — the natural frequency reveals the structural mode, the damping ratio reveals how much energy the system dissipates per cycle. A change in either over time is the leading indicator of bearing degradation, mounting drift, or imbalance.
